title: Zephyrine and the Garden
premise: August Galloway keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories, bottled years, and other impossible things — until prayers start being answered by old gods waking beneath a country that was officially erased from every map a century ago. When August discovers their own childhood memories were sold to the guild, they team up with Zephyrine, a disgraced priestess who can hear the waking gods, to find the Door of Unmaking: the only exit from a nation that no longer exists. The guild's master, Corvane, has been feeding memories to the gods to corrupt them into instruments of power, and he needs August's ledgers — written in August's own blood — to complete the ritual. In the end, August burns the ledgers and gives back what remains of their stolen self, unmaking the door and the country together, choosing love and an unwritten future over power.
about_author: Dominic Sandoval is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed, an experience that taught him how much of a life can live inside paper. He writes fantasy about people caught between what they remember and what they were told to forget, and lives near a coastline that appears on fewer maps each year.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: August's POV. A night of routine work at the Vellum Guild: cataloguing a stolen first kiss, a widow's grief, a soldier's courage. August is meticulous, detached, proud of never stealing for themselves. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as professionalism, cracked when a memory jar whispers August's own name.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the drowned chapel of Saint Verre, Zephyrine prays out of habit and something ancient answers — a voice like roots splitting stone. She flees, terrified, because the gods were declared dead and her order disbanded for saying otherwise. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as she realizes she alone heard it.

chapters.title: Inventory of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: August's POV. Master Corvane orders a full inventory; among the vaults August finds a jar labeled with their own childhood — sold to the guild twenty years ago. Corvane warns them gently not to open it. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-estrangement; the ledger-keeper discovering they are also an entry.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Following the voice, Zephyrine crosses a border that official maps refuse to acknowledge, into Vhalen, a nation erased after a war no one will name. Its towns are inhabited but unmapped, its people half-forgotten even by themselves. Emotional beat: disorientation and strange belonging in a place defined by erasure.

chapters.title: Thief and Priestess
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Zephyrine catches August smuggling guild goods through Vhalen; instead of turning her in, August bargains — she knows the old roads, they know where the guild keeps its secrets. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion giving way to reluctant respect over a fire of burning ledgers.

chapters.title: What the Gods Eat
chapters.summary: August's POV. August deciphers entries showing the guild has been selling memories directly to the waking gods — feeding them human longing to shape what they become. Corvane's plan emerges: a god made obedient is a god made useful. Emotional beat: cold horror; August realizes their bookkeeping has been complicity.

chapters.title: The Choir Below
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the catacombs of Vhalen's capital, Zephyrine hears not one god but many, singing discordantly, some starving, some glutted on stolen feeling. She recognizes one voice as the god she served before the disbanding. Emotional beat: grief for a faith weaponized, and resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: August's POV. Corvane reveals he knows August opened the inventory; he offers to return their stolen childhood in exchange for the blood-ledgers needed to bind the gods. He frames it as mercy. Emotional beat: temptation — identity dangled like bait — and August's refusal born of anger rather than virtue.

chapters.title: Roads That Forget You
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Fleeing the guild's hunters, the pair travels Vhalen's shifting roads, which literally rearrange themselves for those the country doesn't recognize. They must make the land remember them — trading small true memories to wayshrines. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening as they trade pieces of themselves to survive.

chapters.title: The Door of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A dying hermit-priest tells them of the Door of Unmaking, the original wound through which the gods entered the world — passable only by someone the country fully remembers and someone it has entirely forgotten, together. Emotional beat: hope with a terrible price attached; prophecy as burden.

chapters.title: August, Missing Years
chapters.summary: August's POV. August finally opens their own jar and relives fragments: a mother's voice, a garden, the day the guild bought them. The person they might have been accuses them gently. Emotional beat: mourning for a self that never got to exist, and the first honest tears in decades.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Vellum
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Guild hunters corner them in a flooded market-town; Zephyrine calls on a starving god to save them, and it answers too well, devouring the hunters' minds along with their violence. Emotional beat: terror of power's appetite — Zephyrine sees what she could become.

chapters.title: The Price of Listening
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The god she saved now follows her, whispering offers. Corvane contacts her secretly: he'll teach her to command the gods if she delivers August's ledgers. Emotional beat: duty versus love crystallizing — she realizes obedience was always the corruption.

chapters.title: Ledger-Burning
chapters.summary: August's POV. August chooses to burn the blood-ledgers early, freeing hundreds of stored memories into Vhalen's air — the country briefly remembers itself, roads stabilizing, names returning. But the act exposes their location to Corvane. Emotional beat: exaltation and sacrifice; doing right knowing it costs everything.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Guided by the freed memories, they find the garden from August's childhood growing wild beneath Vhalen — the place the Door was first opened, where the gods first tasted human feeling. Emotional beat: tenderness amid ruin; love confessed quietly between two people running out of time.

chapters.title: Corvane Ascendant
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV (only chapter). He completes a partial binding using backup copies of the ledgers, fusing himself with the hungriest god. Power floods him; his human doubts burn away — and with them, any ability to want anything but more. Emotional beat: tragedy of corruption; victory that hollows.

chapters.title: The God Who Remembered Being Loved
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine confronts her old god, now Corvane's weapon, and instead of commanding it, she gives it her most cherished memory freely. It hesitates, remembering devotion rather than hunger. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — she breaks her vows to keep her heart.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Garden
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Corvane descends on the garden with his bound god; August and Zephyrine defend the Door with freed memories as weapons — armies of remembered joy and grief. The battle turns when the country itself, newly remembered, rises against its eraser. Emotional beat: desperate, luminous resistance.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the Door, August realizes only the forgotten can close it from within. They give Zephyrine their last recovered memory — the garden, her face in it — so someone will know why. Emotional beat: farewell without bitterness; identity surrendered as a gift, not a loss.

chapters.title: Through the Door
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. August steps through and begins unmaking the Door — and with it, the boundary that let gods be owned. Corvane, fused to a god now set free, dissolves into ordinary human forgetting. Zephyrine holds the doorframe until the last moment. Emotional beat: climax of loss and release intertwined.

chapters.title: A Country With a Name Again
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Vhalen reappears on maps; its people wake remembering themselves. Zephyrine plants a garden above the sealed wound and teaches a new order not to serve gods but to listen to people. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal; grief transmuted into vocation.

chapters.title: The Gardener Returns
chapters.summary: Final chapter, both POVs converging. On the first mapped morning, a stranger arrives at Zephyrine's garden carrying nothing but a jar of soil and a smile that feels remembered. The Door didn't erase August — it returned them, unwritten and new. Emotional beat: grace; love chosen again without the weight of duty.
